company.name: Kid ASA
company.summary: Kid ASA, together with its subsidiaries, operates as a home textile retailer in Norway, Sweden, Finland, and Estonia. The company designs, sources, markets, and sells a range of home and interior products, including textiles, curtains, bed linens, home accessories, decorations, furniture, and other interior products through retail stores and online platforms. It offers products for bedroom, bathroom, easter, beds, outdoor spaces, table settings, kitchenware, office accessories, children room, loungewear and accessories, and sun protection, as well as lamps, pillows and blankets, and carpets. The company offers its products under the Kid Interior and Hemtex brands. The company was formerly known as Nordisk Tekstil Holding AS and changed its name to Kid ASA. Kid ASA was founded in 1937 and is headquartered in Gullaug, Norway.

narrative.company_headline: 7.5% revenue CAGR, 12.3% EBITDA margin and 1.5x net debt/EBITDA — market cap NOK 5.0bn
highlights: **Consistent growth:** revenue compounded at 7.5% p.a. over 2022–2025, reaching NOK 3,945m
**Margin profile:** pre-IFRS 16 EBITDA margin of 12.3% in 2025A (down from 13.1% in 2022A), EBIT margin 8.7%
**Weak cash conversion:** unlevered FCF of NOK 13m in 2025A, 3% of EBITDA (average 44% over 2022–2025), ROIC 13%
**Balance sheet:** net debt of NOK 1,081m equals 1.5x EBITDA, a conservative leverage level

narrative.market_headline: Peer benchmarking on a consistent basis

threats: Potential **cost spikes in raw material and freight** prices

financial_commentary: **Kid grew revenue by 4.2% in 2025A** to NOK 3,945m, with pre-IFRS 16 EBITDA of NOK 485m (12.3% margin)

**2026E is built on the 2 reported quarters:** revenue +8.1% year-to-date at a 9.0% EBITDA margin (8.2% a year earlier); the rest of the year at +7.2% growth on last year's seasonal margins gives NOK 4,243m (+7.6%) and a 13.1% margin; growth then follows consensus (4 analysts) and fades to 2.0% by 2031E
**EBITDA margin path:** 13.1% in 2026E to 15.3% in 2031E; D&A 3.4% and capex 5.6% normalising to 3.6% of revenue; tax rate 22%
**Unlevered FCF** rises from NOK 216m to NOK 468m over the forecast period (9.1% FCF margin in 2031E)
**Valuation vs peers:** Kid trades at 11.9x LTM EV/EBITDA versus a peer median of 10.5x (+13%) and 19.1x P/E versus 19.7x
**Street view:** consensus target of NOK 139.50 across 4 analysts (+14% vs current price)
narrative.valuation_subtitle: We recommend a HOLD. Our 12-month target price of NOK 126.00 implies +3% upside and a +11% total return including dividend; 10.9x 2026E EV/EBITDA.
narrative.valuation_headline: DCF fair value NOK 125.26, peer multiples NOK 105.82, scenario-weighted NOK 129.60 versus a share price of NOK 122.20 — HOLD
market_implied: **Market-implied WACC 8.7%**, in line with our 8.6%: the price discounts our cash flows at 13bp more than we do
**Market-implied margin:** at our WACC the price is consistent with a 2031E EBITDA margin of 15.1% versus 15.3% in our base case

**Cross-check – medium agreement:** the DCF is 18% above the peer-multiple value (NOK 105.82) and our target is 10% below the consensus of 4 analysts (NOK 139.50); review the growth, margin and WACC assumptions before relying on the target
scenario_commentary: **Bear (25%):** Growth 2pp lower, margin 1.5pp lower, WACC +50bp; revenue CAGR 2.6%, 2031E margin 13.8%, WACC 9.1% gives NOK 80.67 (-34% vs price)
**Base (50%):** Base-case drivers; revenue CAGR 4.6%, 2031E margin 15.3%, WACC 8.6% gives NOK 125.26 (+3% vs price)
**Bull (25%):** Growth 2pp higher, margin 1.5pp higher, WACC -50bp; revenue CAGR 6.6%, 2031E margin 16.8%, WACC 8.1% gives NOK 187.21 (+53% vs price)
thesis: **DCF value of NOK 125.26 per share** (WACC 8.6%, terminal growth 2.0%); terminal value is 76% of EV, implying 9.1x exit EV/EBITDA
**Peer multiples imply NOK 105.82** per share (median of EV/EBITDA, EV/EBIT and P/E-based values)
**Scenarios:** bear NOK 81 / base NOK 125 / bull NOK 187; probability-weighted NOK 129.60
**12-month target price NOK 126.00:** fair value NOK 125.26 (valued at 23.09.2026) rolled forward at the 8.8% cost of equity less NOK 10.00 dividend; expected total return +11%, rating HOLD
multiples_commentary: **Trading at a premium:** 11.9x EV/EBITDA vs 10.5x peer median (13% premium)
**Earnings multiple:** 19.1x trailing P/E vs 19.7x for peers (-3%); 13.0x vs 13.4x on next-twelve-month consensus
**Versus own history:** 11.6x trailing EV/EBITDA is above the 3.5-year median of 9.5x (85% of weeks were cheaper)
**EV/EBITDA-implied value:** NOK 104.65 at the peer median of 10.5x (range 92–111 across the 25th–75th percentile)
risks: **Value drivers:** EBITDA margin ±1pp moves fair value to NOK 111.4–139.2, WACC ±0.5pp to NOK 114.0–138.3 (base NOK 125.26)
**Execution:** the case assumes 7.6% growth in 2026E and margins of 15.3% by 2031E; a return to the 2022–2025 average margin of 14.8% would cut fair value
**Macro:** consumer spending, interest rates and FX can move revenue and the discount rate simultaneously
consensus: **EPS 2026E NOK 6.83 vs consensus NOK 8.16 (-16%):** we are below the 4 analysts – outside the range of estimates; 2027E -22%; our view rests on a 13.1% 2026E EBITDA margin and a 22% tax rate
**Revenue 2026E NOK 4,243m vs consensus NOK 4,230m (+0.3%):** in line by construction – our growth is anchored on consensus, so the differentiated view sits in margins
**Estimate momentum negative:** consensus EPS over the last 90 days 2026E -6.1%, 2027E -6.0%; 2 upward and 6 downward revisions in the last 30 days
multiples_depth: **On next-twelve-month consensus** Kid trades at 13.0x P/E (peers 13.4x), 1.4x EV/Sales (peers 0.9x), 11.0x EV/EBITDA at the LTM margin (peers 9.8x); PEG 0.61 vs 1.12
**Growth and margin explain 61% of the dispersion in peer EV/EBITDA** (8 peers): fundamentals justify 12.0x against the 10.5x median (+15%); the actual 11.9x leaves -1% unexplained. Evidence strong
**Regression-implied value NOK 124.12** per share (NOK 104–144 within one residual standard deviation)
**Cash and payout:** -1.7% levered FCF yield vs 4.2% for peers; 8.2% dividend yield vs 4.2%
**Consensus EPS growth FY1:** +21% for Kid vs +13% for the peer median – the growth the forward multiple is buying
